For Every Indian City • Municipal Transparency Platform

Where did your money go? Check it on the ground, in your own city.

JanMoolya Tracker brings the municipal budget, ward-wise spending and real development work together in one place — not for one city, but for every Indian city. Whether work marked 'Complete' on paper actually happened on the ground — every citizen can check.

Honest data policy: Wherever an official figure is available, it will be marked VERIFIED along with its source. This platform is not linked to any government body. Tagline: Your Tax. Your Ward. Full Account.

⭐ Winning Feature

Mismatch Detector — Paper vs Ground

When work is 'Complete' on paper and almost all the money is spent — but citizens on the ground say 'it never happened' — the system itself raises a ⚠️ MISMATCH flag.

Research

We Asked People First, Then Built It

Team survey • 22–23 Nov 2026 • 17 responses • 52.9% aged 18–24 • 9+ cities. The sample is small, so we honestly call it 'directional' — but the signals are very clear.

88.2%

don't know where to check the municipal budget.

94.1%

never got information about any project's spending. Only 1 person out of 17 succeeded.

70.6%

face civic problems every day — garbage, roads and drainage are part of their daily life.

0%

received a full resolution after complaining. Follow-up is simply missing from the system.

100%

say connecting public money to real work is Important / Very Important.

94.1%

would Definitely / Probably use such a platform — where budget + ward spending + project progress come together.

📷 Photo proof with every report

Citizens told us a complaint without a photo is easy to ignore. Every JanMoolya report carries a photo, and Photo Pehchano AI sorts it into the right category and department.

✓ Paper-vs-ground verification

58.8% of survey respondents asked for citizen feedback on project pages, and 100% called connecting spending to real work Important. So every project shows Paper Status next to Ground Status — with a public Fixed / Not Fixed vote.

🗣️ Bilingual — English / Hinglish

41.2% of people did not understand budget words like Property Tax, Grants and Expenditure. Every page on JanMoolya switches fully between English and Hinglish — use the toggle in the header.

Public money → Ground reality. In one place.

03 • Budget Explorer

Budget Explorer — Department & Ward-wise Spending

Where the money comes from, where it goes department-wise, and how much is allocated vs actually spent in every ward — all three in one place.

📍

Where does public money come from — and where does it go?

Tap any card to see a simple real-life example.

₹

Property Tax

The yearly tax citizens pay on homes and shops. It is the city's own income and funds roads, lights, water and cleaning in your ward.

Share: ~32% of city income

Simple example: You pay ₹6,000 property tax a year. That money joins your ward's pool — part of it pays for the streetlight outside your home, the garbage truck on your street, and road repairs in your lane. If the light stays broken for months, you have every right to ask where your tax went.See example ▾
G

Government Grants

Money sent by the State and Central Government for schemes like roads, drainage, housing and Swachh Bharat. It must be spent on the purpose it was given for.

Share: ~48% of city income

Simple example: The State sends ₹10 Cr as a drainage grant. That money can only be spent on drains — not on parks or salaries. If drains in your ward are still overflowing, the grant was either not spent or not spent well. JanMoolya tracks exactly this gap.See example ▾
≡

Municipal Expenditure

What the municipality actually spends — salaries, contractors, materials and maintenance. JanMoolya compares this spend with work visible on the ground.

Coverage: Tracked ward-by-ward below

Simple example: Records show ₹46 Lakh spent on a road repair in Ward 12 — 96% of its budget. But citizens posted photos of the same broken road and voted 'Not Fixed'. High spend + no ground result = a Mismatch flag. That is expenditure tracking doing its job.See example ▾

    04 • Project Tracker

    Project Tracker — Development Projects & Their Status

    📍

    05 • Report an Issue

    Report an Issue — Photo, Location & Problem

    Survey: 70.6% of people never reported an issue — half of them simply did not know how. Here, reporting takes about 1 minute, and afterwards you get clear next steps and a Tracking ID.

    🔒 Login required to post a report

    Without Login / Sign Up, no report can be posted. Sign in first — after login you will come straight back to this form, and your report will be posted under your name.

    📷 Choose a photo — please blur faces and number plates before uploading


    Your report will appear on this page with a tracking ID.

    ✅ Report received!

    JMT-2026-0000

    1. Use this Tracking ID to check your report's status any time.
    2. The report will be sent to the concerned department — when work starts, the status will become 'In Progress'.
    3. When the work is marked 'Complete', people in your area will be asked for Fixed / Not Fixed verification.
    4. If no action is taken within 7 days, the report auto-escalates and a reminder goes to the Ward Officer.
